title: Trip template
description: What experienced people know about one kind of trip, so a newcomer can plan their own. Times are relative to the trip's anchors, never calendar dates. Nothing personal belongs here: doses taken, ticks, bookings and personal contacts live only in a person's own plan.

id.description: Stable id of the template. Plans record it, so never change or reuse one that has shipped.

name.description: Name shown in the app, in sentence case.

tripType.description: Kind of trip: medical (surgery or other medical stay), hiking, festival (camping festival, Burning Man), conference, other.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what the trip is and who the template is for.

author.description: Optional name or handle of whoever wrote the template. Leave it out to stay anonymous.

version.description: Raised by one each time the template is published again.

asOf.description: Date this snapshot of experience was written (YYYY-MM-DD). Shown beside the advice, because the professionals in charge may have changed their guidance since.

anchors.description: The trip's key dates. A plan sets the real date for each, and every timing in the template counts from them.

label.description: Name of the date, such as Surgery or Arrival.

kind.description: day: a single date (with an optional time in the plan). range: a start and an end date; a `when` refers to the end with `<id>:end`.

phases.description: Named stretches of the trip in time order, such as Pre-op or On the trail. The Today view picks the current one.

summary.description: What this phase is about, in a sentence.

rules.description: Things to do, avoid or limit, each with its reason.

title.description: The rule in a few words, such as No solid food.

detail.description: Exactly what it means in practice.

kind.description: do: something to do; avoid: something not to do; limit: something to keep under a limit.

strength.description: must: required by the professional in charge or for safety; should: strongly recommended; tip: helpful.

meds.description: Medications and health items that are usually in play, with their purpose and typical pattern. A person's actual doses live only in their plan.

name.description: Common name, with the generic name in brackets when it helps.

category.description: What kind of medication or health item it is.

rx.description: Whether it usually needs a prescription.

purpose.description: What it is for, in plain words.

typicalPattern.description: How it is usually taken, such as every 6 hours as needed for the first 3 to 5 days. Never a personal dose.

cautions.description: Interactions or side effects worth knowing about.

packing.description: Gear, supplies and shopping, each with where and when to get it.

category.description: Free grouping shown as a heading, such as Clothing or Cooking.

quantity.description: How many or how much, such as 2 pairs.

obtain.description: Where and when to get the item.

how.description: bring: from home; buy-before: buy ahead and bring it; buy-there: buy on location; rent-there: rent on location; provided: the venue, hospital or organizer supplies it.

where.description: A shop, website or place, if it matters.

byWhen.description: Latest moment to get it, relative to an anchor.

why.description: Why get it that way, such as Fuel can't fly, buy it near the trailhead.

food.description: Phased eating plan: what to eat in each stretch of the trip, with ideas.

name.description: Name of the stage, such as Clear liquids or Trail days.

avoid.description: Foods to stay away from in this stage.

ideas.description: Recipes, products or places to eat.

contactId.description: A contact or place in this template, for a restaurant.

contacts.description: People, organizations and places. Each has a role; the concrete details are optional, so a template can stay abstract.

role.description: What they are to the trip, such as Surgeon, Ranger station or Pharmacy.

whenToUse.description: When to call or go there, such as Fever over 38.5 °C.

logistics.description: Travel, lodging, tickets, permits and the like, with when to sort them out.

byWhen.description: Book or sort it out by then.

daily.description: Options for the daily checklist: activities, appointments, meds, meals and tasks. A person picks and ticks them in their own plan.

repeat.description: How often it comes up while its window is open. once: on the window's first day.

optional.description: True when it is a suggestion rather than part of the routine.

medId.description: The med in this template it is about.

contactId.description: The contact or place it involves.

sources.description: Where the reasons come from, listed once and cited by id.

kind.description: instructions: from the professional or organizer in charge; guideline: official or professional guidance; study: research; article: other writing; forum: a community discussion; personal: the author's own experience.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Plans refer to it, so it never changes.

offset.description: Hours, days or weeks from the anchor: -12h, -14d, +6w, 0d.

anchorRef.description: An anchor id, or `<id>:end` for the end of a range anchor.

window.description: From one moment to another, relative to an anchor. `to` may use a different anchor through `toAnchor`. Without `to` it is a single moment.

toAnchor.description: Anchor for `to`, when it differs from `anchor`.

when.description: When something applies: a window relative to an anchor, or a whole phase.

phase.description: A phase id; applies for the whole phase.

why.description: The reason behind the item, which motivates people to follow it when it isn't obvious.

basis.description: official: the instructions of the professional or organizer in charge; evidence: a guideline or study; experience: what past participants learned.
